items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: actually he was working with Benny Moten at that time

ctx.x: Now talk to us about when you first started with Basie.

Well I was with Basie’s first band in 1932 or 33, which was short-lived, and actually he was working with Benny Moten at that time. But Moten was having a lot of problems with getting work. So Basie got a job in I think it was Little Rock, Arkansas. And he came to Little Rock and I was there, and I worked with him there in that band.
How did you meet? How did you audition for him or get that spot?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Bennie Moten took New York by storm when he came here.

ctx.x: Man, they tell me when they came in, those chorus girls went crazy because they wasn't too fast for them, you know. They said they were doing everything because the tempo was right. They said, "Where did this band come from? We ain't never heard no tempos like this." And that's another thing that made it great for them, you know. Bennie Moten took New York by storm when he came here. That's when he had -- Basie was still in the band and Ben Webster was in the band, Eddie Barefield, people like that, you know, and…

were in," and all the bands would play like up in here. So you can't keep that up all night. If you dance one or two times with tempos up in there, you're tired. So they had a variety of tempos and I think that's another thing that had them in, you know.
